item.text: The initial Verus run reaches Rust initialization checks before deeper proof checking. The failures are all the same pattern: tracked row stores are assigned inside an atomic proof closure, so the compiler cannot establish that they are initialized before executable code borrows them. I’m restructuring those proof-only tracked moves so initialization is explicit while preserving the executable statements and contracts.
